change.para: application request handling uses one thread per worker process; threads and thread_stack_size configuration and Ruby thread hooks are removed.
libunit and Go request handling are simplified to use one thread; worker process state is separated from ports.
configuration API responses include application startup error details.
status reports worker pool max, spare, busy, and idle counts; connection statistics and running and starting worker fields are removed.
application and global status report total, active, queued, completed, and failed requests, response status classes, and request latency in milliseconds.
request latency statistics include approximate cumulative P95 and P99 percentiles; global percentiles use merged application latency samples.
application and global process statistics count abnormal worker exits; normal recycling and prototype exits are excluded.
thread startup, configuration mapping alignment, MurmurHash2 shifts, and empty-string formatting are corrected.
README documentation describes features and quick start; the migration guide and packaging references are removed.
Java, Node.js, and Perl application support and related packages and container images are removed.
listeners pass requests directly to fixed applications and targets; built-in routing, configuration variables, and NJS expressions are removed.
built-in TLS, static file serving, reverse proxying, upstream load balancing, and access logging are removed.
certificate and JavaScript module control APIs and the OpenSSL, PCRE, and NJS dependencies are removed.
standard Forwarded header processing with listener forwarded.trusted IP/CIDR rules replaces legacy client_ip and X-Forwarded-* configuration.
unused job, cache, buffer filter, buffer pool, fiber, memory zone, vector, time parsing, and sendfile code is removed.
initial AppServe release with runtime configuration and multi-language application hosting.
daemon, packages, services, default paths, and server identification use AppServe names; application API and binding identifiers are retained.
